theme: 3 terms on collections: storing many values in Swift

terms.definition: A collection that stores values in order and lets you read each one by its position.
terms.example: The array keeps the tags in order, so the screen looks right.

terms.definition: A collection that links each unique `key` to a `value`, so you can look up data by name.
terms.example: Store the tag colors in a dictionary, with the tag as the `key`.

terms.definition: A collection that stores unique values in no particular order and ignores duplicates.
terms.example: Turn the list into a set, and the duplicate tags are gone.

video.description:
Learn to talk about collections in Swift: Array, Dictionary and Set, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Array - A collection that stores values in order and lets you read each one by its position.
Dictionary - A collection that links each unique `key` to a `value`, so you can look up data by name.
Set - A collection that stores unique values in no particular order and ignores duplicates.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Array, Dictionary & Set in English | Duplicate Tag Bug Chat | Day 5
landscape.description:
Explain Array, Dictionary and Set in Swift by listening to a real bug-fix chat between two iOS devs.
영어 버그 수정 대화로 array, dictionary, set 표현을 익혀요.

Array - A collection that stores values in order and lets you read each one by its position.
한국어: 값을 순서대로 저장하고 위치로 읽을 수 있는 컬렉션

Dictionary - A collection that links each unique `key` to a `value`, so you can look up data by name.
한국어: 고유한 키마다 값을 연결해 이름으로 데이터를 찾는 컬렉션

Set - A collection that stores unique values in no particular order and ignores duplicates.
한국어: 중복 없이 고유한 값을 순서 없이 저장하는 컬렉션

In this video, Mina and Jake fix a duplicate tag bug in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Morning, Jake. How is the tag screen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not great. Users see the same tag twice on the profile screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do you store the tags?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In an array of strings. The array keeps the order, so the screen looks right.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. But an array allows duplicates.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, swift appears twice. That is the bug.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use a set. A set ignores duplicates.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. Why does `tags[0]` not compile?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A set has no order, so there is no `index` to read.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. I will turn the set into an array to show it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where do you keep the tag colors?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In two arrays, one for names and one for colors, matched by `index`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Risky. Use a dictionary: tag name as the `key`, color as the `value`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the dictionary links each tag to its color?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, and lookup is fast. But the result is optional.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, the `key` might be missing. I will add a default.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Remember, a dictionary has no order, like a set.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. Array for order, set for unique tags, dictionary for the colors.
Use a set, and duplicate tags disappear.
